01 · What we measured

What we measured, and what the numbers cannot tell you

Sup measured 97 protein coffee and shake brands, 2,790 creator posts, 294 of the brands' own top posts and 4,511 live Meta ads between 29 December 2025 and 28 June 2026; no survey was involved.

  • Every brand in the category (97)
    97 US brands selling protein shakes, protein coffee, protein powder, energy drinks, functional coffee and protein bars.
  • Creator posts tagging them (2,790)
    2,790 creator posts on Instagram and TikTok tagged one of the brands in the window; the 1,500 top Instagram posts and 640 top TikTok posts by views form the creator pools the tier tables stand on.
  • The brands' own posts (294)
    294 of the brands' own top posts by views and by engagement, 100 on Instagram and 194 on TikTok.
  • Meta Ad Library (4,511)
    4,511 live ads across 54 advertising brands at the end of the window, and the 100 longest-running creatives analysed in full.

Gemini read the 400 most-viewed and most-engaged creator posts and recorded each one's hook, format, pillar, creative style, production effort and opening three seconds; the hook breakdown covers 368 of the 400.

Definitions and worked examples
Engagement rate: likes plus comments on a post, divided by its views, as a percentage
Example: The median creator post by an Instagram account with 10k to 100k followers in this category came to 0.33% across 568 posts.
Views per follower: creator views on the brand's posts, divided by the summed followers of the creators who tagged it
Example: Legion drew 13,697,297 creator views; divided by the followers of the creators who tagged it, that is 2.01 views per follower.
Top 10% threshold: the view count that 90% of posts in the tier fall below
Example: For Instagram creators with 10k to 100k followers here, a post above 27,334 views is in the top 10%; above 455,276 it is in the top 1%.
Against the median: a group's median views divided by the median views of all 400 analysed posts (30,258)
Example: Talking head videos had a median of 102,351 views, which is 3.38 times the median analysed post.

What this data cannot tell you

No fees, sales or attribution

We see what was posted and how it performed. We do not see what a creator was paid, whether a post drove sales, or which post a buyer saw first. Views per follower and engagement per post are the honest proxies and are named as proxies throughout.

One window, not a trend

Everything here was measured between 29 December 2025 and 28 June 2026. A brand that launched in July is not in it, and a number can move by the next edition.

Instagram images carry no view count

Instagram does not report views on images and carousels, so view-based figures stand on video posts. Engagement figures cover every post.

Strategy detection is inference

The strategies section reads posting patterns, captions and ads for the signs of a named strategy. It is a strong signal, not a contract we have seen.

Categories are judgement calls

Which brands belong in this category, and which sub-category each sits in, is a decision we made and can revise.

How Sup measures a category

02 · The shape of the market

Ten brands take most of the attention, and 15 brands get none

The ten most-tagged protein coffee and shake brands took 71.7% of all creator views across 97 brands between 29 December 2025 and 28 June 2026, and the top brand alone took 16.3%.

82 of the 97 brands (84.5%) had at least one creator post tagging them in the window; 15 brands (15.5%) had none. The median active brand had 17 creator posts. 33 brands (34.0%) worked with 20 or more unique creators.

Instagram carried 76.7% of the creator posts and 73.7% of the creator views; TikTok carried 23.3% of the posts and 26.3% of the views. The category is an Instagram category first, with TikTok punching slightly above its post count on views.

Nearly half of all creator posts, 47.9%, came from accounts with 1k to 5k followers, and 10.9% from accounts with over 50k. The category runs on very small creators in volume.

54 brands (55.7%) were running Meta ads at the end of the window and 41 of them had at least one ad older than 30 days; the median advertiser had 25 live ads.

What to do with itAttention is concentrated at the top and spread thin below it, so a new brand should expect to build from small creators in numbers rather than one big name.

03 · The league table

The league table: every brand ranked by creator views

Legion was the most-tagged protein coffee and shake brand, with 151 creator posts and 13,697,297 creator views between 29 December 2025 and 28 June 2026.

Alani Nu had by far the most creator posts, 500 from 330 unique creators, and finished second on views with 12,550,615. Garden of Life reached rank 3 on four posts, because one of them drew 7,008,662 views on its own.

The table ranks on creator views because views are what the whole category is competing for. Sort it by creator posts, unique creators or views per follower to see a different story: TRU Bar, Protein Works and Legion lead on views per follower, and PRÉS worked with 17 creators from a following of 3,179.

04 · Engagement and views by creator tier

Engagement and views by creator tier

On Instagram, protein coffee and shake creators with under 10k followers earned a 0.86% median engagement rate across 486 posts, against 0.2% for creators with 100k to 500k followers across 227 posts (29 December 2025 to 28 June 2026).

Views run the other way. The median Instagram post by a creator under 10k followers reached 1,185 views; by a creator with 10k to 100k followers, 5,351; by one with 100k to 500k, 23,941; by one with 500k to 1M, 94,947. A brand trades reach for engagement as it moves up the tiers.

TikTok views in this category are low outside the top posts. The median TikTok post by a creator with 10k to 100k followers reached 1,975 views and the top 10% passed 20,399, against 27,334 for the same tier on Instagram. The TikTok engagement edge for small accounts, 2.05% against 0.12%, is real, but it sits on small view counts.

The top 1% on Instagram starts at 29,125 views for creators under 10k followers, 455,276 for 10k to 100k, and 786,140 for 100k to 500k. Those are the posts worth copying, and the thresholds a brand should set as its scale trigger.

What to do with itSet the target per tier before briefing: a micro creator's post that passes 27,334 views on Instagram is a top 10% result here, and one that passes 455,276 is a top 1% result worth repeating.
What counts as a good post here

A post above 5,001 views is top 10% for a creator with under 10k followers in this category; above 29,125 it is top 1%.

A post above 27,334 views is top 10% for a creator with 10k to 100k followers in this category; above 455,276 it is top 1%.

A post above 124,225 views is top 10% for a creator with 100k to 500k followers in this category; above 786,140 it is top 1%.

A post above 452,164 views is top 10% for a creator with 500k to 1M followers in this category; above 5,184,308 it is top 1%.

A post above 474,534 views is top 10% for a creator with over 1M followers in this category; above 1,201,485 it is top 1%.

05 · Hooks and formats that win

Hooks and formats that win

Talking head videos were 4.0% of the 400 analysed protein coffee and shake creator posts but earned a median of 102,351 views, 3.38 times the median post (29 December 2025 to 28 June 2026).

Day in the life was the most common format, 137 of the 400 analysed posts (34.2%), with a median of 26,400 views, a little under the median post. Recipes were 15.0% of posts at a median of 42,301 views, 1.4 times the median. The formats that over-deliver are the small ones: talking heads at 3.38 times, get-ready-with-me at 2.75 times on seven posts, tutorials at 2.33 times on eleven, and hauls at 1.55 times on sixteen.

By opening hook, POV and skit set-ups led on count (65 posts, 17.7%) but sat at 0.87 of the median. A tutorial promise in the first line (27 posts) reached a median of 57,280 views, 1.89 times the median; a price or value reveal (9 posts) reached 124,984, 4.13 times; a challenge (8 posts) 65,600, 2.17 times.

The look is creator-filmed: 92.8% of the analysed posts were UGC style, 51.5% were medium production effort and 47.8% low. A face is on camera in the first three seconds in 76.1% of the 368 posts with a hook breakdown, the hook is carried by voice and picture together in 74.7%, the payoff lands at the end or on the loop in 52.2%, and 55.2% cut fast with four or more cuts in the first ten seconds. The median analysed post runs 45 seconds and the mean hook score is 7.4 out of 10.

The six patterns below are the hook and format pairings that stand on five or more posts from several creators; six more looked strong but did not clear that bar, and they are listed after.

What to do with itBrief the small formats with the big lift, talking heads and recipes with a promised how-to, rather than the crowded day-in-the-life default.

The 6 patterns that keep winning

Each pattern is a hook and format pairing that stands on five or more posts from several creators, with the live posts that prove it.

1Recipe or ProcessTutorial Promise10k to 100k followers · Instagram

Recipe: say let's make it, then mix the drink on camera

The creator says "let's make" the drink in the first second and then makes it, pour by pour, in a car park, a kitchen or a gas station. It fits this category because the product is an ingredient here: the drink people want to copy is a dirty soda, a protein mojito or an iced latte built on the can or the creamer. The four videos below are all a promise then a pour, and the smallest account in the group is the one that travelled furthest.

How to brief it

A kitchen counter, a car, or a fountain drink station; phone propped or held by a friend; natural light

  1. 0 to 3s: the creator says "let's make" the drink and shows the can or tub
  2. 3 to 8s: the first pour over ice, close on the cup
  3. 8 to 18s: the second ingredient and the stir; the colour change is the moment
  4. last 3s: the first sip and a one-line verdict, cup to camera

Call to action: Ask the viewer which flavour to make next; put the recipe in the caption

Six hooks to hand a creator

  • Let's make a dirty protein coffee at the gas station
  • Let's turn this energy drink into a mojito to go
  • Three ingredients and this shake tastes like dessert
  • Let's make the iced latte everyone keeps asking about
  • Let's make a protein pudding with one scoop and milk
  • Let's make my 40 grams of protein breakfast bowl

Copy it when a post passes 455,276 views (the top 1% for micro creators (10k to 100k followers) on Instagram). Scale when 2 posts beat 27,334 views (the top 10% for micro creators (10k to 100k followers) on Instagram). Stop when 3 posts stay under 5,351 views (a typical post for micro creators (10k to 100k followers) on Instagram).

How to brief it

A cafe, a car, a hallway by the front door; one actor, sometimes a second pair of hands; no voiceover needed

  1. 0 to 3s: the scene is set in one line of text on screen or one spoken line
  2. 3 to 8s: the product enters as the prop, not the subject
  3. 8 to 15s: the beat that makes the joke or the point
  4. last 3s: the sip, the bite, or the exit, held for a second

Call to action: Ask "who else does this?" in the caption; keep the brand tag in the first comment

3Talking HeadAudience Callout10k to 100k followers · Instagram

Talking head: the health reason first, the product second

A micro creator talks to camera and opens with the reason, a diagnosis, a parent's worry, a professional's habit, before the product appears. It fits this category because most shoppers here are buying for a reason (protein target, energy, a condition) and a face saying the reason out loud is the fastest way to earn the recommendation. How to brief it

The place the named person lives their day: trail, kitchen, desk, bar cart; face first, then product

  1. 0 to 3s: the callout, spoken to camera or as the on-screen line
  2. 3 to 8s: the product in the named person's setting
  3. 8 to 18s: the use, in real time, no montage
  4. last 3s: the line again as a sign-off with the product in hand

Call to action: Ask the named group to tag a friend who is one of them

Six hooks to hand a creator

  • Beverage girls, this protein coffee is your new 3pm
  • If you hike, here's the protein bar that survives the bag
  • Mums who never eat breakfast, this shake is for you
  • Friday night protein people, this cocktail has 20 grams
  • Night-shift workers, this energy drink got me through
  • Runners, this is what I drink the morning before a race

Copy it when a post passes 786,140 views (the top 1% for mid-size creators (100k to 500k followers) on Instagram). Scale when 2 posts beat 124,225 views (the top 10% for mid-size creators (100k to 500k followers) on Instagram). Stop when 3 posts stay under 23,941 views (a typical post for mid-size creators (100k to 500k followers) on Instagram).

Patterns that looked good but stand on too few posts

  • POV skits by creators over 1M followers looked strong on six posts, but two are one creator and no brand briefs that tier.
  • Taste tests by mid-size creators looked strong on five posts, but the biggest is a laptop review tagged to a brand with the same name.
  • Recipes with a curiosity hook on TikTok: all five posts are one creator's series and none has stable media.
  • Before-and-after day-in-the-life videos on TikTok stand on nine posts, most from one creator's weight-loss series.
  • Recipes with a bold claim: seven of the twelve posts are one creator's ice-cream series, and the recipe pattern already covers it.
  • Product-in-action posts by mid-size creators: the biggest post in the group is about a different product, and the rest are thin.

Three scripts to fill in

The "I always get asked" recipe
  1. Open with: I always get asked how I make my [breakfast bowl, iced coffee, pudding].
  2. Show the base: the yogurt, the coffee or the oats, already in the bowl or cup.
  3. Add the protein: one scoop or one pour, and say the grams out loud.
  4. Add the texture: something crunchy or creamy on top, filmed close.
  5. Finish with a store-bought topping and the first bite to camera.
The post it comes from
Advice before a milestone
  1. Open with the milestone: [the race, the birthday, the move] is next week.
  2. Say who you asked: a coach, a doctor, a parent.
  3. Tip one is the product: the shake before [the thing], shown as you do it.
  4. Tips two to five are life advice, one line each, filmed across the day.
  5. Close on the morning of the milestone with the product in hand.
The post it comes from
The small-win skit
  1. Set up the hard moment in one line of text on screen: the 5am alarm, the long shift.
  2. Cut to you with the drink and the sunglasses, saying nothing.
  3. Let a trending sound carry the joke; no voiceover.
  4. One beat where the drink is the reason you are fine.
  5. End on the sip, held for a full second.

06 · The creators behind the category

The creators behind the category

Of the 1,419 creators who posted about a protein coffee and shake brand in the top creator pools, 1,067 (75.2%) posted once in the window and 123 (8.7%) posted three or more times about the same brand (29 December 2025 to 28 June 2026).

149 creators (10.5%) tagged two or more brands in the window. That shared bench is where a brand finds creators who already film this category: heathergets_healthy tagged eight brands, takingmylifebackat42 six.

The bench is small by follower count. Creators with 10k to 100k followers were 42.0% of all posting creators and made 42.3% of the posts; creators under 10k were 35.4% and made 34.7%; creators with 100k to 500k were 17.5%. Accounts over 500k were 5.1% of creators between them, so the category's reach is built by many small accounts, not a few large ones.

The top creators by views are led by single viral posts rather than programmes: the biggest, 12,714,042 views, is a laptop review that tags Legion's account and is not category content; the next is a 7,008,662-view day in the life tagged to Garden of Life.

What to do with itStart with the shared bench and the two lists below; they are creators the category has already proven, and most have posted about a brand only once, so they are open to a second.

A retainer signal.

A creator with one post about one brand in the window is an organic or gifting signal: they tried it, they posted, they moved on. A creator with three or more posts about the same brand is a retainer signal, a paid or ambassador relationship. Both are signals from public posts, not proof of a contract.

07 · What the category is running

What the category is running

Strategies are inferred from posting patterns, captions and ads; see the methodology page for how each one is detected.

8 of 97 protein coffee and shake brands showed signs of Earned Organic Mentions and 8 showed signs of UGC for Brand Feed between 29 December 2025 and 28 June 2026; 24 brands (24.7%) showed at least one strategy we can detect.

Six brands showed signs of Always-On Creator Retainers, led by Alani Nu with 16 creators posting three or more times each across five months. Six showed signs of Press & Brand Trips, again led by Alani Nu, which had 37 unique creators tag it inside a seven-day window starting on 19 June 2026.

Four brands ran a Long-Term Brand Ambassador, three UGC for Paid Ads, and three an Affiliate / Commission Programme (Protein Works had 14 creator captions with codes or links). Six brands ran three strategies at once: Clean Simple Eats, Alani Nu, Myprotein, Protein Works, Ghost and Legion.

What to do with itMost brands here run nothing we can see; a single always-on retainer group, which six brands already run, would put a new entrant in the top quarter of the category on visible strategy.

08 · Creator content in Meta ads

Creator content in Meta ads

54 of 97 protein coffee and shake brands (55.7%) were running Meta ads at the end of the window, 4,511 live ads in total, and 40.3% of those ads had run for more than 60 days.

3,477 of the live ads were older than 30 days, 1,818 older than 60 and 991 older than 90; the median advertiser's ads had run for 23.2 days. Video made up 51.8% of live ads, carousels 26.0% and images 22.2%.

The creative style is far more polished than the creator posts: cinematic creatives were 25.9% of live ads by weight, polished brand 17.7%, and creator-style UGC only 11.5%. Five of the 18 advertisers with enough classified creatives run mostly UGC.

Among the 100 longest-running creatives, 66 were still live after 60 days. Carousels over-index among the survivors (index 1.15 on 33 creatives) and low-effort creatives too (1.11 on 37); polished brand creatives under-index (0.67 on 18). Javvy ran the most live ads, 511, then RYZE with 483 and Humantra with 465; Protein Works kept 205 of its 230 ads past 60 days.

Advertisers whose creatives are mostly UGC (five brands) drew a median of 230,193 creator views; advertisers with mostly polished creatives (13 brands) drew 244,703; brands with no live ads (43) drew 16,796. That is an association between advertising and creator attention, not a cause.

What to do with itThe category's ads do not yet look like its creator posts; a brand that runs creator-style video in Meta while the others run cinematic cuts is testing something 89% of advertisers here are not.

09 · Brand feeds versus creator posts

Brand feeds versus creator posts

On TikTok, the protein coffee and shake brands' own top posts drew a median of 271,850 views against 21,300 for the top creator posts, 12.8 times as many (29 December 2025 to 28 June 2026).

That reversal belongs to a few brands. Premier Protein's own recipe videos drew 67,700,000, 64,900,000 and 51,700,000 views, and Perfect Bar's 27,100,000; the brand-own TikTok feed in this category is a recipe channel that creators are not matching.

On Instagram the picture flips. The brands' own top posts earned a median of 610 likes and comments against 1,176 for the top creator posts, 1.9 times as many for the creators; Instagram brand images carry no view count, so views cannot be compared there.

The brand feeds are 29.8% promotional and 19.9% relatable content; carousels are 18.0% of the top brand posts, skits 16.2% and talking heads 14.3%. 32.7% of the brand posts carry a paid partnership label. Alani Nu placed 30 posts in the top 100 brand feed posts and Clean Simple Eats 29.

What to do with itOn TikTok, copy what the brand feeds already prove: fast recipe videos with the product as the ingredient. On Instagram, creators out-engage the brands, so put the budget there.

12 · What to do with this

What to do with this

If you have no creator posts yet

  1. Brief creators under 100k followers in numbers, not one big name.
    Creators with under 100k followers made 77.0% of the category's posts and small accounts hold the engagement edge, 2.05% on TikTok against 0.12% for accounts with 100k to 500k followers.See the table
  2. Start with a recipe that promises the how-to in the first line.
    Recipes with a tutorial promise reached a median of 61,731 views across 17 posts, 2.17 times the median, and the biggest one came from an account with 2,977 followers.See the table
  3. Put a face and a reason in the first three seconds.
    76.1% of the top posts open with a face on camera, and talking heads by micro creators reached a median of 161,245 views on five posts.See the table
  4. Run one always-on retainer group before any single big deal.
    Only six of 97 brands show a retainer group and 123 creators already post three or more times about one brand, so the creators are used to it.See the table

If you are already in the top 25

  1. Move your Meta creative towards the creator posts that already work for you.
    Cinematic creatives are 25.9% of live ads and UGC only 11.5%, while 92.8% of the top creator posts are UGC style.See the table
  2. Treat your own TikTok as a recipe channel.
    The brands' own top TikTok posts drew 12.8 times the views of the top creator posts, led by Premier Protein's recipe videos.See the table
  3. Set the scale trigger at the top 1% for the tier, and copy what passes it.
    On Instagram that is 455,276 views for a creator with 10k to 100k followers and 786,140 for 100k to 500k.See the table
What we would test first

We would test the recipe pattern first, with eight to ten creators under 100k followers on Instagram and a handful of accounts under 10k on TikTok, each briefed to say "let's make" the drink in the first second and pour it somewhere real: a car, a kitchen, a gas station. The bar is the top 10% for the tier, 27,334 views on Instagram; anything past 455,276 gets cloned across the group the following week.

Three things in this data surprised us. First, the category's own feeds beat its creators on TikTok, and by a distance: Premier Protein's recipe videos drew tens of millions of views each while the median top creator post drew 21,300. The brands have found the format; most creators have not. Second, the ads and the creator posts belong to different worlds. 92.8% of the top creator posts are creator-filmed, yet cinematic creatives make up 25.9% of live ad weight, polished brand 17.7%, and UGC 11.5%. The category is paying for a look its audience does not choose. Third, attention is concentrated and empty at the same time: ten brands take 71.7% of creator views, 15 brands have no creator post at all, and only 24 show a strategy we can detect. There is room in this category for a brand that briefs small creators on a recipe and keeps at it.

Matt Greenwell · September 2026

Questions people ask

What is a good engagement rate for a protein coffee or shake creator post on Instagram?

A creator with 10k to 100k followers posting about a protein coffee and shake brand earned a median engagement rate of 0.33% between 29 December 2025 and 28 June 2026, across 568 posts. The median post reached 5,351 views and the top 10% passed 27,334. Creators under 10k followers earned 0.86% on 486 posts.

Do small creators beat big creators in protein coffee and shakes?

On engagement, yes. Creators under 10k followers earned a 2.05% median engagement rate on TikTok, 17.1 times the 0.12% of creators with 100k to 500k followers, across 326 protein coffee and shake posts between 29 December 2025 and 28 June 2026. On views the bigger accounts win: a median of 23,941 views on Instagram for 100k to 500k followers against 1,185 for under 10k.

What content formats work for protein coffee and shake brands on Instagram and TikTok?

Day in the life was 34.2% of the 400 analysed creator posts at a median of 26,400 views; recipes were 15.0% at 42,301 views; skits 8.8% at 25,912; taste tests 7.2% at 18,800. The formats with the biggest lift were talking heads (median 102,351 views on 16 posts) and tutorials (70,500 on 11), measured between 29 December 2025 and 28 June 2026.

What influencer strategies are protein coffee and shake brands running?

Earned Organic Mentions (8 brands), UGC for Brand Feed (8), Always-On Creator Retainers (6), Press & Brand Trips (6) and Long-Term Brand Ambassador (4), detected from posting patterns, captions and ads across 97 brands between 29 December 2025 and 28 June 2026. 24 brands showed at least one strategy.

How many protein coffee and shake brands run Meta ads?

54 of 97 brands (55.7%) had live Meta ads on 28 June 2026, 4,511 ads in total. Video made up 51.8% of live ads, and 40.3% of the ads had run for more than 60 days.

Which protein coffee and shake brand gets the most creator posts?

Alani Nu had the most creator posts, 500 from 330 unique creators, between 29 December 2025 and 28 June 2026. Legion had the most creator views, 13,697,297 from 151 posts.

Where does this data come from?

Sup measured every brand in the protein coffee and shake category: 2,790 creator posts tagging them on Instagram and TikTok, 294 of the brands' own top posts, 4,511 live Meta ads, and a Gemini content analysis of the top 400 creator posts, between 29 December 2025 and 28 June 2026. No surveys. It does not include creator fees, sales or attribution.
